references.text: The parallel text in [ref:Mark 14:13|Mark 14:13] describes the same event where Jesus sends two disciples into the city and tells them they will meet a man carrying a water jar, and that they should follow him.

In [ref:Matt 26:18|Matt 26:18], Jesus gives similar instructions to go into the city to prepare for the Passover meal, although the details about the man with the water jar are not explicitly mentioned in Matthew.

In [ref:Luk 19:30-32|Luke 19:30-32], Jesus shows a similar prophetic foreknowledge when he sends disciples to fetch the colt, and everything happens exactly as he said—this pattern of Jesus' supernatural knowledge of future events parallels Luke 22:10.

In [ref:1 Sam 10:2-3|1 Sam 10:2-3], Samuel gives Saul prophetic signs about whom he will meet on the way, in a similar manner to how Jesus here gives the disciples a specific sign (the man with the water jar) they should look for.

The immediate context in [ref:Luk 22:8-9|Luke 22:8-9] shows that Jesus sent Peter and John to prepare for the Passover meal, and they asked him where they should do it—verse 10 is Jesus' answer with the specific sign they are to look for.

[ref:Luk 22:11-13|Luke 22:11-13] is the direct continuation where Jesus gives further instructions on what they should say to the owner of the house, and the disciples find everything exactly as Jesus had said—a confirmation of his foreknowledge.
